strDesc: Finds Target for Prospector gold Fetch plot.
[us] [says] [them] [has] a strong back, and [us-asks] if [them] would like to earn good money cracking rocks.

Your approach nearly scares the man out of his shoes. Tools and rocks spill from his hands as he whips around to face you, a look of genuine terror in his eyes.

"Got damn! Liable to get shot creepin around like that. Yer quiet as a hunt cat, anyone ever tell you that? Lordy loo."

The harried man retrieves a yellowed rag and mops copious sweat from his brow as he regards you with narrowed eyes.

"If yer one of them Azikiwe pricks I'll tell you what I told the last one: I ain't sellin my claim! There's color in these rocks yet. I can smell it."

Despite the man's aggressive demeanor, his singing makes you doubt his capacity for violence. As you grope around for a reply you notice more peculiarities of the lone spacer.

The gold motif of the ship extends to his wardrobe, each piece a fierce yellow, including the high G compression leggings you glimpse between his shoes and the cuffs of his pants. As if that weren't enough, his fingers and mouth are stained to a permanent orange, signs of an exclusive diet of cigarettes and Nacho Fiesta Trenchers.
strTooltip: IT'S GOLD TIME

strDesc:
"Ha! Name's Jacob Waltz, and I'm one of them whatchamacallits," he pauses, then lights up. "En-tree-panours. Hung my own shingle, you see."

"In fact, I'd love to hire you for a little favor if yer willin and able. You seem able enough from where I'm standin. Are ya willin?"
strTooltip: IT'S GOLD TIME

strDesc:
Look it's simple: what I crave is gold. Shiners. Pay dirt. That sweet auric chloride. Hell, I'd even take chlorauric acid in a pinch, long as she's yella. I'll give you good money per nugget. Above rate, because I know somethin these poor saps don't."

Jacob has a strange tic you've never seen before. Periodically he will tilt his head back, widen his eyes, purse his lips, and suck in air as if through an invisible straw.

"So what'll it be? You in?" he asks.
strTooltip: IT'S GOLD TIME

strDesc:
When you explain that you aren't interested in helping out at this time, Jacob assures you that you can take your sweet time. "Oh I'm as patient as the hills. Been at this a while already, and as long as the corps keep out of my business, I'll be at this till the veins run dry. And I'm always willin to pay better than either of the damn factions fightin to monopolize all the rocks at Ceres."

His appraising eyes gives you a once over, "Come find me later... when you've got gold on you, or one o'them shiny Halvorson mining lasers, or a legit Radar, or hell, a whole PDC".
strTooltip: IT'S GOLD TIME

strDesc: When you agree to trade your effort for his money, Jacob can't help busting into a little spacer jig before wincing a bit at the toll his toil has taken on his own body. "Perfect! I'll take all the gold you can get yer hands on. Check the veins of the shiniest asteroids, either in my rocks in this here patch, or the thousands over by Ceres, where CCRE and the Galilean Confederacy wage war with all their claim beacons, bullets, and bombs." He sizes you up, quirking an eyebrow, "In fact, if you head that way, I'd pay through the teeth for one o'them ergo-nomical-type Halvorson mining lasers." The idea perks him right up, and he extends his wishlist, "Hell, if you've got the gumption to cozy up to one side of that war or the other enough to squeeze a radar out of 'em, or hell, a proper PDC I can mount to keep the suits away, I could make you fithy rich." He licks his teeth, "Say... $25k per nugget and for one laser, $80k each for a radar and a PDC? Y'hear me?"
strTooltip: IT'S GOLD TIME

strDesc: Jacob brightens up at the chance to jabber on about his particular know-how, "What do you want to know?"

Jacob elaborates story after story about how the CCRE, a coalition of pirates-turned-corporate suits in their cushy Ring Station, 'the Mint', fancy to monopolize the metallurgy industry System-wide, and aren't shy about using PMCs (aka mercenary ship crews) to do so.

Unfortunately, the Galilean Confederacy—a united batch of hard-scrabble laborers and revolutionaries who recently won their sovereignty by actually overthrowing their corporate overlords—has brought all their knowhow harvesting from Jupiter's moons and Trojan asteroids into the Belt to dip their hand in the pot from the surface colony on Ceres.

Conspiratorially, he adds that many, himself included, believe it's all propped up as a proxy tussle for dominance between Xinhua from the Inner Planets and Titan from the Outer Planets.

strTitle: Ask How to Acquire Ship Weapons & Sensors
strDesc:
Jacob explains how both the CCRE at Ring Station (BCRS) and the Galilean Confederacy folks at Port Mojave, Ceres (BCER) pay out in scrip and faction standing for anyone willing to serve their interests: Selling them minerals, claiming asteroids by planting beacons on their behalf, or committing violence against enemy ships or pirates.

After proving yourself be earning enough favor, they'll sell you more advanced weapons, sensors, and ammunition. Each faction has their own brands, with different strenghts and weaknesses. Xinhua's fancy-pants tech excels in railguns and sensors, but Titan offers the best missiles and PDCs.

But they only sell the goodies using their own internal currency, "scrip", which is really just a racket to lock you into the system of working for them, earning from them, buying from them, at exorbitant exchange rates if you care to get any real money you can use elsewhere.

Jacob tells you the best yield is in the deposits found deep in the core, not just the surface regolith.

The shiny rocks, M-Class, tend to have the most precious output, including gold of course, followed by S-Class, the stony sort, which also sometimes give up gold, just less often. Dark rocks, C-Class sometimes have water and ice, but otherwise mostly just carbon and silicates, which might be worthwhile in bulk, but takes more work.
You resume playing.
